The first accused in S.T.No.181 of 2008 on the files of the Court of the Judicial Magistrate of First Class-II, Perambra, filed this revision petition challenging the concurrent finding of conviction and sentence passed by the courts below under Sections 16 (1) (a) (ii) r/w Section 7(iii) of the Prevention of Food Adulteration Act,1954 and Rule 50 (1) of the Prevention of Food Adulteration Rules,1955.

sentences.text:
2. Heard.
3.
The prosecution allegation can be briefly stated thus:-
On 22.10.2007 at about 3.00 p.m., PW1, the Food Inspector purchased 600 gram of dried grape (raisins) from the first accused.
The second accused was the distributor and the third accused was the manufacturer.
After sampling as per rules, one sample was sent to the Public Analyst for analysis.

After analysis, the Public Analyst submitted Ext.P13 report stating that the sample contained damaged raisins more than 2% and hence it did not conform to the standard prescribed for raisins as per the PFA Rules, 1955 and was therefore adulterated.
Thereafter, on the request of the accused, the second sample was sent to the Central Food Laboratory for analysis.
Ext.P21 certificate of the Central Food Laboratory would show that the sample did not conform to the standard prescribed for raisins under the PFA Rules and was therefore adulterated.
It is further alleged that the revision petitioner did not have a valid licence under the PFA Rules to sell the food items.
4. Before the trial Court, PW1 to PW5 were examined and Exts.P1 to P28 were marked for the prosecution.
DW1 to DW3 were examined and Exts.D1 to D3 were marked for the revision petitioner.
5. The trial court, after appreciating the evidence, found the revision petitioner guilty for the sale of adulterated food items.
The trial court also found that the revision petitioner sold the food item without having a valid licence as per the PFA Rules.
In the appeal, the appellate court set aside the conviction and sentence passed by the trial court in respect of the sale of the adulterated food item.
However, the conviction and sentence passed by the trial court, for the sale of the food item without having a valid licence, were confirmed by the appellate court.
The courts below concurrently found that the revision petitioner sold the food item without having a valid licence under the PFA Rules.

sentences.text: Having gone through the relevant inputs, I do not find anything to hold that the concurrent finding by the courts below, that the revision petitioner sold the food item without having a valid licence under the PFA Rules, suffers from any infirmity, warranting interference by this Court.

In the said circumstances, the concurrent finding by the courts below that the revision petitioner committed the offence under Sections 16 (1) (a) (ii) r/w Section 7(iii) of the Prevention of Food Adulteration Act,1954 and Rule 50 (1) of the Prevention of Food Adulteration Rules,1955, does not warrant any interference by this Court.
6.

entities.text: Prevention of Food Adulteration Act,1954 and
entities.label: STATUTE

sentences.text: As regards the sentence, the learned counsel for the revision petitioner has pleaded for leniency.
The revision petitioner was aged 50 years during the relevant period.
The revision petitioner is presently aged 58 years.
There is no previous conviction against the revision petitioner.
Considering the facts and circumstances of the case, I am of the view that the sentence in this case can be awarded as provided under second proviso to Section 16 (1) of the PFA Act.

Accordingly, the sentence awarded by the courts below can be modified and reduced to imprisonment till the rising of the court and a fine of Rs.500/- (Rupees five hundred only) and in default to simple imprisonment for ten days under Sections 16 (1) (a) (ii) of the Prevention of Food Adulteration Act r/w Rule 50 (1) of the Prevention of Food Adulteration Rules, to secure the ends of justice.
Accordingly, I order so.
In the result, this revision petition stands allowed in part as above.
The revision petitioner shall surrender before the trial court on 1.4.2016 to suffer the sentence.

Sd/-
B. SUDHEENDRA KUMAR JUDGE Scl/09.02.2016
